title: When a Street Changes
sentences: The street I grew up on is barely recognisable now.
The garage became a cafe, and the cafe later became flats.
Property prices rose steadily for about fifteen years.
The families who had lived there longest were the first to leave.
It would be easy to describe this as simple decline, and inaccurate.
The street is safer, cleaner and considerably better served than before.
What has gone is harder to name than what has arrived.
There is nobody left who remembers my grandmother.
A neighbourhood is partly a set of buildings and partly a shared memory.
Only one of those two things can be rebuilt with money.
